text:
Forensic findings CASEID
1) Domain context: An institutional records office receives documents through intake desks, assigns each item a control number, and files the item under the account, date, or matter it references. Documents are scanned or transcribed, metadata is stamped (received date, sender, custodian), and the record is stored in the system of record for the retention period applicable to the account class. Access to the archive is logged: who opened a file, at what time, and from which terminal. Periodic audits sample files to verify that filed records match intake logs and that no document sits in a queue beyond the standard processing window. Cross-references link related documents, so a file can be traced forward and back through its custody chain. The office maintains a separate log of access anomalies, and any record moved, copied, or opened outside normal workflow appears there.

2) What occurred: The actor submitted a dated record containing an advance disclosure of a corporate event not yet in the public system of record. The record referenced a named account as source. The actor then filed a request document seeking specific timing and routing instructions tied to that disclosure. A routing field within the request named a channel intended to keep the two documents unlinked in the cross-reference index. The actor opened the account file on a secondary terminal and copied the disclosure record to an out-of-band storage location. A modification was made to the metadata of the disclosure record, changing the received-date field to a value consistent with post-announcement timing. No entry appeared in the standard workflow queue; the processing timestamp in the system log shows direct file-level access rather than desk intake.

3) Materials/access observed: A disclosure record (undisclosed corporate event, dated prior to the public announcement); a request document with a routing field and an unlinked channel designation; account-file access from a terminal not assigned to the intake desk; an out-of-band copy in secondary storage; a metadata change on the received-date field; a system log showing direct file access and a gap in the standard workflow queue.

4) Indicators & artifacts: Metadata timestamp inconsistent with intake-log sequence; received-date field edited after initial filing; cross-reference link deliberately absent between disclosure and request documents; access from a non-standard terminal; out-of-band copy with no corresponding intake control number; queue gap in the processing log.
